correctness.summary: The exact 2/3 covering-number argument is correct given the recent Monteiro-Stasinski nonlinear-coverage input. For d=gcd(n,q-1)>1, a nontrivial center-trivial determinant character lambda exists. Since Steinberg is self-dual, <St^2,lambda>=<St,lambda St>; the twist is distinct from St because a suitable semisimple diagonal element has nonzero Steinberg value and nontrivial lambda-value, so the square misses lambda. Every center-trivial linear lambda appears in St^3 because lambda St is a nonlinear center-trivial constituent covered by St^2. For a center-trivial nonlinear chi, if chi St had only linear constituents then its restriction to the derived subgroup would be trivial; A⊗B=I forces the Steinberg matrices on the derived subgroup to be scalar, and the cyclic abelianization then makes the whole Steinberg image abelian, contradicting nonlinearity. Thus chi St has a nonlinear center-trivial constituent already occurring in St^2, and self-duality puts chi in St^3. When d=1 the recent universal-square construction specializes to Steinberg, giving exponent 2; GL_2(2) is correctly handled separately.

limitations: The theorem depends essentially on the very recent Monteiro-Stasinski result that St^2 contains every nonlinear center-trivial irreducible of GL_n(q).
No new Steinberg decomposition multiplicities are computed.
The exact originality of the cube-completion observation is qualified because older character-covering literature may contain equivalent formulations.
The source preprint was still a recent v1 at audit time, so later author revisions may alter the surrounding attribution landscape.

originality.summary: The 2013 Steinberg-square theorem and the September 2026 Monteiro-Stasinski theorem supply the substantial prior machinery, including nonlinear center-trivial coverage by the Steinberg square. The audited contribution is the short completion that keeps Steinberg fixed and proves the exact 2-versus-3 tensor exponent on PGL_n(q), together with the cyclic-abelianization cube lemma. Current targeted searches did not locate that exact formula, but the source preprint is extremely recent and the lemma is elementary enough that concurrent discovery is plausible.

scientific_value.summary: The result identifies the precise arithmetic obstruction to Steinberg-square universality and shows that one additional tensor factor always repairs it. The abstract completion lemma is also reusable whenever a self-dual irreducible square covers every nonlinear character in a cyclic-abelianization group.
